# Celeris 파일별 설명과 코드 대조 — CD2

분류별 개수: 일치 364; A 3; B 14; C 48; D 0; E 4; F 1; H 49; X 0.

## 1 요약

이 보고서는 AI가 작성한 원문 대조 기록이다. 코드 기준은 `models/Celeris/raw/source_code/Celeris-WebGPU/`의 `ebca435` 사본이다. 코드 경로는 이 디렉터리를 기준으로 한다. `NOTE/` 경로는 `models/Celeris/`를 기준으로 한다. 원자료와 현재 노트는 수정하지 않았다. 모델과 브라우저는 실행하지 않았다.

요청은 `docs/source/**`의 문서를 91개로 적었다. 실제 사본에는 86개 파일이 있다. 이 수는 해당 디렉터리 아래 일반 파일의 재귀 목록에서 셌다. 별도 `docs/architecture/`에는 5개 문서가 있다. 이 보고서는 파일별 문서 86개와 구조 문서 5개를 대조한다. 두 집합의 합계는 91개다. 이 합계를 파일별 설명 문서 91개라고 부르지 않는다.

파일별 문서 86개는 모두 텍스트다. 빈 파일과 그림만 있는 문서는 없다. 외부 라이브러리 문서 3개와 표시 전용 skybox·duck·model 셰이더 문서 6개도 판정 행을 둔다. 해당 코드 내부는 사용자의 제외 범위이므로 판독하지 않았다. 표시용 Handler와 파이프라인의 호스트 계약은 대조했다.

바인딩 번호와 연결 자원의 대조는 각 바인딩에 행을 둔다. 같은 처리의 반복 차이는 한 행으로 묶는다. 문서의 소유자 설명과 해당 기능의 상세 설명은 같은 행에 함께 인용할 수 있다. 개발 권고는 H로 구분한다. 권고문에 포함된 현재 동작은 구현 대조 행을 함께 적용한다.

원문에 없는 식을 문서가 보증한다고 해석하지 않는다. 3절은 구체적인 기본값·수식·검사를 생략한 항목을 C로 기록한다. E는 코드 결함 후보다. 같은 판 문서·자원 연결·다른 코드 경로와의 모순 및 반대 근거를 함께 적는다. 실행 결과를 확인한 결함으로 쓰지 않는다.

현재 노트 14개에는 관련 서술의 유지·수정안을 적었다. 문서 오기의 주요 항목은 지형 평탄화 셀 수·Pass3B 도함수 호출 순서·숫자 인수 생략 처리·설정 키다. 표준 Pass2의 퇴적물 확산을 비활성으로 적은 노트도 수정안에 포함했다. overlay의 과거 인수 누락은 해당 문장의 도입판과 이후 수정판을 구분했다.

논문 2017·2020은 이전 구현을 설명한다. 이 작업의 직접 대조 대상은 파일별 설명 문서다. 논문 전체의 쪽·식 감사는 이 보고서에 포함하지 않는다. 논문 식을 새로 전사하지 않았으므로 PDF 쪽 이미지는 이 작업에서 열지 않았다.

저장 후 검사에서 1–5절 순서와 고유 ID 483개를 확인했다. 파일별 색인 86개에는 빠진 파일이 없다. 일치 이외의 고유 ID 119개는 5절에 각각 한 번 나타난다. 공백 구분 형식의 원문 줄 인용 12,573회를 현재 파일 또는 인용한 git 판의 줄과 문자열 대조했다. 이 검사에서 문자열 불일치는 0개였다. 이 수는 반복 인용을 포함한 출현 수다. 인용 문자열 검사 자체를 수식의 물리 검증으로 취급하지 않는다.

When the two boundaries transverse to the incident-wave boundary are periodic, it applies periodic-boundary direction fitting before upload. The fitting uses the active forcing span `boundaryLength - 2 * ds`, matching `BoundaryPass.wgsl` coordinates from index `1` to index `N-2`. Each fitted component selects an integer number of along-boundary waves and sets `k_parallel = sign(k_parallel_raw) * 2*pi*N / activeBoundaryLength`, so the component phase matches at both active ends of the boundary. The root CELERIS add path resets start/end endpoint state after applying the structure while preserving the cross-section values for repeated structures. ``<br>docs/source/js/agent_controls_js.md:107 `  `<br>docs/source/js/agent_controls_js.md:108 `` The bridge also sets the root design interaction mode. | CD2-352 | docs/source/js/main_js.md:7 `` `main.js` is the application orchestrator. It initializes WebGPU, loads scenario inputs, allocates every major GPU resource, creates shader pipelines and bind groups, runs the simulation loop, manages the render loop, handles most UI events, and triggers export/readback operations. ``<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:8 `  `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:9 ` This is the file that turns the collection of shader passes into an actual coastal-wave model. `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:10 `  `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:11 ` ## Startup Responsibilities `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:12 `  `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:13 ` The initialization path loads config, bathymetry, waves, optional overlays, optional initial surfaces, and model assets. It then: `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:14 `  `<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:15 `` - Requests the WebGPU adapter/device and configures the canvas. | CD2-366 | docs/source/js/main_js.md:105 `` - Export buttons for images, GIFs, JSON config, simulation surfaces, and nested-grid boundary time-series rectangle outputs. While nested-grid output is active, every active rectangle is drawn as a black outline through the existing `txDraw` overlay. The rectangle uses lower-left model-grid `j` indices for capture, but the overlay y coordinate is inverted when drawing because the shared draw canvas is already vertically flipped before upload. The nested output UI edits the legacy/first rectangle; additional rectangles can be configured through `nestedGridOutput_rectangles`. The nested output UI also exposes `nestedEtaWriteThreshold`, which trims quiet leading samples from the final downloaded files during readback rather than changing the GPU sampling pass. ``<br>docs/source/js/main_js.md:116 `` - Nested-grid boundary output dynamically allocates four compact edge textures for each active output rectangle when the user starts capture. If `nestedGridOutput_rectangles` is absent or has no enabled entries, the legacy scalar `nestedGridOutput_*` fields produce one rectangle exactly as before. Additional rectangle prefixes default to `nestedGridOutput_file_prefix`, `nestedGridOutput_file_prefix2`, `nestedGridOutput_file_prefix3`, etc., so a base prefix of `gridD` produces `gridD`, `gridD2`, and `gridD3`. Requested sample counts above the configured maximum are capped by increasing each rectangle's output `dt` and logging a warning. Each rectangle uses its own uniform buffer, bind group, and four output textures. Readback/download waits until no rectangles are still actively sampling, then completed rectangle textures are read and released; optional threshold trimming drops quiet leading rows while preserving shifted/global times in the boundary files. `` | js/main.js:1944 `     function getNestedGridOutputRectangleSpecs() { `<br>js/main.js:1945 `         const basePrefix = | CD2-379 | docs/source/js/README.md:3 ` These files are the browser-side control plane for the simulator. They do not perform the heavy numerical work directly; they load data, allocate GPU resources, create bind groups, dispatch WGSL passes, copy textures, manage UI state, and export results. `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:4 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:5 `` The central file is `main.js`. Most other modules either feed it data, create a narrow WebGPU binding contract for a shader, or read data back out of the GPU. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:6 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:7 ` ## Core Orchestration `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:8 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:9 `` - `main.js`: application bootstrap, WebGPU initialization, simulation loop, UI event handling, render loop, and output triggers. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:10 `` - `constants_load_calc.js`: default config, config loading, and derived constants. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:11 `` - `Config_Pipelines.js`: compute and render pipeline creation. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:12 `` - `Create_Textures.js`: WebGPU texture and buffer allocation helpers. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:13 `` - `Copy_Data_to_Textures.js`: CPU-side packing of bathymetry, waves, initial state, and tridiagonal coefficients into GPU textures. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:14 `` - `Wave_Generator.js`: UI-selected sine and TMA boundary-wave row generation before upload to `txWaves`. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:15 `` - `Run_Compute_Shader.js`: generic compute dispatch and texture-copy helpers. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:16 `` - `Run_Tridiag_Solver.js`: PCR-based implicit solver orchestration. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:17 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:18 ` ## Data I/O And UI `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:19 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:20 `` - `File_Loader.js`: loads grids, wave files, overlays, image bitmaps, cube maps, and optional user files. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:21 `` - `File_Writer.js`: exports textures, images, GIFs, configs, time surfaces, and readback data. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:22 `` - `display_parameters.js`: updates DOM status/config panels and redirects console logs into the page. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:23 `` - `Time_Series.js`: reads tooltip and point-gauge values back from the GPU. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:24 `` - `Model_Loaders.js`: loads simple scene models and prototype glTF assets. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:25 `` - `site.js`: currently inert placeholder. ``<br>docs/source/js/README.md:26 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:27 ` ## Handler Files `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:28 `  `<br>docs/source/js/README.md:29 `` `Handler_*.js` modules define WebGPU bind-group layouts and bind groups for matching WGSL passes. | CD2-382 | docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:7 `` `js/main.js` creates a `frame()` function that is called by `requestAnimationFrame`. Each frame may contain multiple simulation timesteps. The variable `render_step` is adjusted at runtime so the application can do more compute between renders when the GPU is fast, but back off when the browser needs more responsiveness. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:8 `  `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:9 ` Important per-frame responsibilities: `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:10 `  `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:11 `` - Handle pending UI/config changes (`html_update`). ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:12 `` - Handle mouse edits (`click_update`). ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:13 `` - Handle requested disturbances (`add_Disturbance`). ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:14 `` - Run `render_step` simulation timesteps. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:15 ` - Pack render data into half-float textures. `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:16 ` - Draw either the 2D view or 3D view. `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:17 ` - Extract tooltip/time-series data. `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:18 ` - Save images, GIF slices, or output surfaces if requested. `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:19 `  `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:20 ` The loop also periodically flushes the WebGPU queue to reduce the risk of long-running GPU command accumulation. `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:21 `  `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:22 ` ## Timestep Sequence `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:23 `  `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:24 ` The core timestep is a finite-volume update plus optional dispersive correction: `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:25 `  `<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:26 `` 1. `Pass0.wgsl` computes neighbor water depths around each cell. This is a helper texture for dry/wet logic in the flux pass. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:27 `` 2. `Pass1.wgsl` or `Pass1_HighOrder.wgsl` reconstructs face states from cell-centered state and bathymetry. It writes face depth, face velocity, and scalar values. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:28 `` 3. `SedTrans_Pass1.wgsl`, if sediment is enabled, reconstructs sediment concentration at faces. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:29 `` 4. `Pass2.wgsl`, `Pass2_HighOrder_HLLC.wgsl`, or `Pass2_HighOrder_HLLEM.wgsl` computes numerical fluxes through cell faces. The current high-order path selects HLLC. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:30 `` 5. `Pass_Breaking.wgsl`, if enabled, computes breaking age/intensity and eddy-viscosity flux helpers. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:31 `` 6. In COULWAVE mode, `Pass3A_COULWAVE.wgsl` and `Pass3B_COULWAVE.wgsl` build auxiliary terms and pack them into `txCW_groupings`. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:32 `` 7. `Pass3_NLSW.wgsl`, `Pass3_NLSW_Spherical.wgsl`, `Pass3_Bous.wgsl`, or `Pass3_COULWAVE.wgsl` computes flux divergence, friction, pressure forcing, breaking/diffusion terms, scalar decay/dispersion, and the predictor/corrector update. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:33 `` 8. `BoundaryPass.wgsl` applies boundary conditions and wet/dry cleanup to the explicit/intermediate state. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:34 `` 9. For Boussinesq/COULWAVE, `Update_TriDiag_coef*.wgsl` refreshes implicit-solver coefficients when required. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:35 `` 10. `Run_Tridiag_Solver.js` dispatches `TriDiag_PCRx*.wgsl` then `TriDiag_PCRy*.wgsl`. NLSW mode skips the solve by copying the intermediate state to `txNewState`. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:36 `` 11. `BoundaryPass.wgsl` is run again after the implicit solve. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:37 `` 12. Sediment bottom update may run, which changes `txBottom`, cumulative bed-change textures, near-dry flags, and tridiagonal coefficients. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:38 `` 13. History textures are shifted and `txNewState` becomes `txState`. ``<br>docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md:39 ` 14. Diagnostics run: face velocities are refreshed, means and wave heights are updated, and render variables are packed. ` | js/main.js:2222 `     async function frame() { `<br>js/main.js:2223 `  `<br>js/main.js:2224 `         // flush the GPU command queue every 10 minutes to prevent memory issues and potential GPU connection loss `<br>js/main.js:2225 `         nowFlush = Date.now(); Data rows store `[eta, hu, hv, 0]` per station. JavaScript uploads one shared time bracket to `BoundaryPass`; the shader handles interpolation along the boundary coordinate. ``<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:122 `  `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:123 ` ## Nested-Grid Boundary Output Textures `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:124 `  `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:125 `` Nested-grid boundary output dynamically allocates four temporary `rgba32float` textures per active output rectangle when capture starts: ``<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:126 `  `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:127 ` - South and north output textures have width equal to the rectangle x-edge station count and height equal to the capped number of output samples. `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:128 ` - West and east output textures have width equal to the rectangle y-edge station count and height equal to the capped number of output samples. `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:129 `` - Each pixel stores `[eta, hu, hv, 0]`. ``<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:130 `  `<br>docs/architecture/DATA_AND_TEXTURES.md:131 `` `ExtractNestedBoundaryTimeSeries.wgsl` writes these textures only at requested output times. Multi-rectangle output reuses the same shader and texture layout once per active rectangle, with independent uniform buffers, sample indices, thresholds, prefixes, and deferred readbacks. | CD2-387 | docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:3 `` Configuration is a flat JavaScript object, `calc_constants`, exported by `js/constants_load_calc.js`. Example `config.json` files override the defaults. Derived values are then computed in JavaScript and uploaded to WebGPU uniform buffers. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:4 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:5 ` ## Loading Order `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:6 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:7 ` The typical loading flow is: `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:8 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:9 `` 1. `calc_constants` starts with defaults in `constants_load_calc.js`. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:10 `` 2. `loadConfig()` fetches the selected example `config.json`, if one is selected. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:11 `` 3. `init_sim_parameters()` merges uploaded or example config values onto the defaults. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:12 ` 4. Derived values are recalculated: dispatch counts, timestep, Boussinesq coefficients, inverse grid spacing, boundary reflection indices, canvas/render dimensions, sediment coefficients, and colorbar layout. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:13 ` 5. Uniform buffers are updated from the resulting values. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:14 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:15 ` There is no schema validator. Unknown keys may be ignored, and missing keys fall back to default JavaScript values if the code path reads them. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:43 `` - `west_boundary_type`, `east_boundary_type`, `south_boundary_type`, `north_boundary_type` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:44 `` - `BoundaryWidth` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:45 `` - `incident_wave_type` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:46 `` - `incident_wave_H`, `incident_wave_T`, `incident_wave_direction` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:47 `` - `numberOfWaves` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:48 `` - `ts_west_file`, `ts_east_file`, `ts_south_file`, `ts_north_file` for boundary type `5` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:49 ` - river stage/discharge fields for flood scenarios `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:50 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:51 `` For `incident_wave_type == 0`, `main.js` treats the UI values as a single sine-wave component, converts height to amplitude with `H / 2`, converts direction from degrees to radians, sets `numberOfWaves` to 1, and reuploads `txWaves`. For `incident_wave_type == 1`, `Wave_Generator.js` builds a cached TMA directional spectrum from the same height, period, and direction controls, sets `numberOfWaves` to the generated component count, and reuploads `txWaves`. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:52 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:53 `` Boundary type `5` reads `eta`, `hu`, and `hv` from side-specific text files. In custom local runs, the Start Here panel can upload west/east/south/north boundary time-series files directly; uploaded files override the matching `ts_*_file` path. All active type-5 boundary files must use the same time vector. Station locations are interpreted as model x/y coordinates for Cartesian grids and absolute longitude/latitude degrees for `grid_type == 2`. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:57 `` - `nestedGridOutput_i0`, `nestedGridOutput_j0`, `nestedGridOutput_i1`, `nestedGridOutput_j1` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:58 `` - `nestedGridOutput_start_time`, `nestedGridOutput_end_time`, `nestedGridOutput_dt` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:59 `` - `nestedGridOutput_max_samples`, `nestedGridOutput_sample_count`, `nestedGridOutput_sample_index` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:60 `` - `nestedGridOutput_trigger`, `nestedGridOutput_active` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:61 `` - `nestedGridOutput_rectangles` for optional multi-rectangle output specs ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:62 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:63 `` The scalar settings define the legacy rectangle whose four edges are sampled as `eta/hu/hv` output files compatible with boundary type `5`. Existing configs that only use these scalar fields remain valid. When `nestedGridOutput_rectangles` contains enabled entries, each entry can define `i0`, `j0`, `i1`, `j1`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `dt`, `eta_threshold`, and `file_prefix`/`name`. If a rectangle omits `file_prefix`, the default is `nestedGridOutput_file_prefix` for the first rectangle, then that base plus numeric suffixes for later rectangles, for example `gridD`, `gridD2`, `gridD3`. Each rectangle's sample count is capped at `8192` by increasing its output `dt` and logging a warning. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:64 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:65 ` Sediment: `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:66 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:67 `` - `useSedTransModel` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:68 `` - `sedC1_shields`, `sedC1_criticalshields`, `sedC1_erosion` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:69 `` - `sedC1_fallvel`, `sedC1_n`, `sedC1_bedloadMPM` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:70 `` - `sedTurbDispersion`, `sedBreakingDispersionCoef` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:71 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:72 ` Rendering and interaction: `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:73 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:74 `` - `surfaceToPlot` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:75 `` - `colorMap_choice`, `colorVal_min`, `colorVal_max` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:76 `` - `GoogleMapOverlay`, `IsOverlayMapLoaded` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:77 `` - `renderZScale` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:78 `` - `showArrows`, `arrow_scale`, `arrow_density` ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:79 ` - design-component friction constants `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:80 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:81 ` ## Uniform Coupling `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:82 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:83 `` Many WGSL files declare their own `Globals` struct with only the values that shader needs. Those struct layouts are filled from JavaScript uniform-buffer packing logic in `main.js`. The coupling is positional and byte-layout sensitive; adding a field to a shader `Globals` struct requires updating the corresponding JavaScript buffer writer. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:84 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:85 `` The same config value can appear in multiple shader `Globals` structs. For example, `delta`, `base_depth`, grid dimensions, and inverse grid spacings are repeated across hydrodynamic, sediment, boundary, render, and tridiagonal shaders. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:86 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:87 ` ## Derived Values `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:88 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:89 `` `init_sim_parameters()` computes values that are not meant to be edited directly: ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:90 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:91 `` - `dt` from grid spacing, gravity, base depth, and Courant-style settings. For `grid_type == 2`, `dx` is `dlon` in degrees, `dy` is `dlat` in degrees, and the timestep uses the minimum spherical physical spacing across the latitude range. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:92 `` - `DispatchX`/`DispatchY` from grid size and workgroup size. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:93 `` - `Px`/`Py`, the PCR iteration counts. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:94 `` - Inverse grid spacing and powers such as `one_over_d2x`, `one_over_d3x`, and `one_over_dxdy`. ``<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:95 ` - Boundary reflection/shift indices. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:96 ` - Render/canvas ratios and colorbar coordinates. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:97 ` - Sediment settling/erosion coefficients from configured material properties. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:98 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:99 ` When a scenario behaves oddly, check whether the value is directly loaded from JSON or derived after loading. The latter may be overwritten every time UI changes trigger recalculation. `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:100 `  `<br>docs/architecture/CONFIGURATION.md:101 `` For `grid_type == 2`, spherical-coordinate support is currently NLSW-only. The setup path forces Boussinesq/COULWAVE, high-order reconstruction, sediment transport, and the Cartesian breaking model off for that mode. `` | js/constants_load_calc.js:438 `         var | CD2-389 | docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:3 ` The project follows a handler pattern: each compute or render pass has a JavaScript handler file that creates the bind-group layout and bind group expected by one or more WGSL shaders. `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:4 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:5 `` The important rule is simple: binding numbers are the interface. The order in the handler must match the `@group(0) @binding(N)` declarations in WGSL, and the resources passed by `main.js` must match what the handler expects. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:6 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:7 ` ## Handler Responsibilities `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:8 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:9 ` Most handler files do three things: `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:10 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:11 `` 1. Define a `create_*_BindGroupLayout(device)` function. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:12 `` 2. Define a `create_*_BindGroup(...)` function. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:13 ` 3. Map JavaScript texture/buffer arguments to numbered WebGPU bindings. `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:14 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:15 `` The handlers usually do not dispatch work themselves. Dispatch is handled by `Run_Compute_Shader.js`, `Run_Tridiag_Solver.js`, or the render code in `main.js`. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:16 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:17 ` ## Shader Responsibilities `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:18 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:19 `` WGSL files declare a matching `Globals` struct and matching texture/storage bindings. They assume: ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:20 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:21 ` - All textures have the dimensions implied by config. `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:22 ` - Storage outputs are separate from sampled inputs unless JavaScript explicitly uses a temporary texture and later copies it. `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:23 `` - Workgroup sizes are usually `16 x 16`, except time-series extraction and some fullscreen render paths. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:24 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:25 ` ## Why Temporary Textures Are Common `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:26 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:27 `` WebGPU does not allow reading and writing the same texture in a single pass in the way many numerical algorithms would like. The code therefore uses temporary textures such as `txtemp_boundary`, `txtemp_Breaking`, `txtemp_bottom`, `txtemp_PCRx`, and `txtemp_WaveHeight`, then copies results into canonical textures after dispatch. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:28 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:29 ` This pattern is especially visible in: `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:30 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:31 `` - `BoundaryPass`: writes temporary water/sediment/breaking outputs, then JavaScript copies them into state textures. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:32 `` - `Pass_Breaking`: writes temporary breaking values, then JavaScript copies into `txBreaking`. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:33 `` - `CalcMeans` and `CalcWaveHeight`: write temporary diagnostics before replacing the running diagnostic textures. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:34 ` - PCR solver passes: repeatedly alternate coefficient and solution textures between iterations. `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:35 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:36 ` ## Shared Layouts `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:37 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:38 ` Some handlers are intentionally shared across shader variants: `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:39 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:40 `` - `Handler_Pass1.js` works for both standard and high-order reconstruction. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:41 `` - `Handler_Pass2.js` works for standard, HLLC, and HLLEM flux variants. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:42 `` - `Handler_Pass3.js` works for NLSW, Boussinesq, and COULWAVE main integration shaders because all three use the same broad binding layout. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:43 `` - `Handler_Tridiag.js` works for standard and COULWAVE PCR variants, although the standard WGSL files do not use every binding declared by the handler. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:44 `` - `Handler_UpdateTrid.js` works for both standard and COULWAVE coefficient-update shaders. ``<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:45 `  `<br>docs/architecture/WEBGPU_BINDING_PATTERN.md:46 ` Shared layouts simplify pipeline selection but increase the risk of unused or misleading bindings. | CD2-391 | docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:3 `` The `docs/` directory includes technical papers that explain the lineage of this codebase. These notes are a practical guide to how the papers relate to the source, not a substitute for reading the papers. ``<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:4 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:5 ` ## Lynett Et Al. 2026 `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:6 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:7 ` The WebGPU paper describes the browser-based direction of Celeris: a static web application that performs interactive nearshore wave modeling on the client GPU. That matches the current repository architecture: no server-side compute, no build step, and WGSL compute shaders for the numerical passes. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:8 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:9 ` Relevant implementation connections: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:10 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:11 ` - WebGPU compute replaces earlier graphics/engine-specific GPU shader approaches. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:12 ` - The model supports nonlinear shallow water, Boussinesq, and higher-order/COULWAVE-style formulations. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:13 ` - The code uses a hybrid finite-volume/finite-difference strategy: finite-volume fluxes for the hyperbolic part, finite differences and implicit solves for dispersive terms. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:14 ` - Interactivity is part of the model design: bathymetry edits, disturbances, design components, map overlays, and time-series probes are not afterthoughts. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:15 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:16 ` ## Tavakkol And Lynett 2017 `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:17 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:18 ` The 2017 Celeris work is the conceptual ancestor for the GPU-accelerated Boussinesq model. It used earlier GPU shader technology rather than browser WebGPU, but the numerical structure is recognizable in this repository. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:19 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:20 ` Relevant implementation connections: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:21 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:22 ` - The explicit finite-volume update is split from dispersive Boussinesq corrections. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:23 ` - Moving shoreline/wet-dry logic is central to the solver. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:24 ` - Parallel Cyclic Reduction is used for tridiagonal systems in the implicit dispersive solve. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:25 ` - Interactive visualization and rapid scenario feedback are core goals rather than post-processing steps. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:26 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:27 ` ## Tavakkol And Lynett 2020 `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:28 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:29 ` The 2020 Celeris Base work moved the interactive model into a more accessible application environment and emphasized user workflows such as map overlays, gauges, and immersive visualization. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:30 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:31 ` Relevant implementation connections: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:32 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:33 ` - The WebGPU version keeps the same spirit of interactive scenario design, but implements it as a static browser app. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:34 `` - The UI, overlay imagery, time-series gauges, and export features in `main.js`, `File_Loader.js`, `File_Writer.js`, and render shaders continue that workflow direction. ``<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:35 ` - Sponge/boundary handling, visualization, and GPU resource management are as important to the application as the equation kernels. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:36 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:37 ` ## Practical Reading Order `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:38 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:39 ` If you are modifying numerical kernels: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:40 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:41 ` 1. | CD2-392 | docs/source/js/constants_load_calc_js.md:20 `` Nested-grid boundary output settings are also stored here under the save-data parameters. `nestedGridOutput_i0/j0/i1/j1`, `nestedGridOutput_start_time`, `nestedGridOutput_end_time`, and `nestedGridOutput_dt` define the legacy single rectangle-edge output capture and remain backward compatible with existing configs. The optional `nestedGridOutput_rectangles` array can define additional rectangles, each with `i0`, `j0`, `i1`, `j1`, optional timing fields, optional `eta_threshold`, and optional `file_prefix`/`name`. If the array is missing or has no enabled entries, the runtime uses the scalar fields exactly as before. The runtime caps each rectangle's sample count to `nestedGridOutput_max_samples`, currently `8192`, by increasing output `dt` and logging a warning. `nestedEtaWriteThreshold` optionally trims leading quiet samples from final boundary files when the readback finds that eta magnitude on any rectangle edge first exceeds the threshold; rectangle-specific `eta_threshold` values override it. `` | ## 4 노트 대조와 수정안

지정된 현재 노트 14개의 관련 서술을 대조했다. 노트 파일은 수정하지 않았다. ‘유지’는 선택한 원문 범위에만 적용한다. 노트 전체를 검증했다고 확대하지 않는다.

## 5 차이 결론

판정 원장에는 고유 ID 483개가 있다. 아래 119개 행은 일치 이외의 판정에 각각 하나의 결론을 붙인다. 파일 수와 판정 행 수를 구분한다.

문서의 판 날짜는 해당 문장의 git blame 도입판으로 적는다. 이후 커밋이 다른 단락만 바꾼 경우에도 문장의 도입판을 구분한다. overlay 문장은 984091f에서 작성됐다. 바로 다음 커밋 bf8db50은 호출 인수를 수정했다. 두 커밋의 날짜는 모두 2026-05-24다.

D는 0개다. 같은 시점의 코드나 같은 문서 묶음의 모순으로 가를 수 있는 항목은 B로 분류했다. 외부 원문의 계수·식 번호와의 새로운 동일성 주장을 하지 않았으므로 X는 0개다. 논문 성능·이론 계보·개발 권고는 H다.

| CD2-391 | docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:3–50 | H 코드 대조 대상 아님 | docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:3 `` The `docs/` directory includes technical papers that explain the lineage of this codebase. These notes are a practical guide to how the papers relate to the source, not a substitute for reading the papers. ``<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:4 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:5 ` ## Lynett Et Al. 2026 `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:6 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:7 ` The WebGPU paper describes the browser-based direction of Celeris: a static web application that performs interactive nearshore wave modeling on the client GPU. That matches the current repository architecture: no server-side compute, no build step, and WGSL compute shaders for the numerical passes. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:8 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:9 ` Relevant implementation connections: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:10 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:11 ` - WebGPU compute replaces earlier graphics/engine-specific GPU shader approaches. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:12 ` - The model supports nonlinear shallow water, Boussinesq, and higher-order/COULWAVE-style formulations. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:13 ` - The code uses a hybrid finite-volume/finite-difference strategy: finite-volume fluxes for the hyperbolic part, finite differences and implicit solves for dispersive terms. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:14 ` - Interactivity is part of the model design: bathymetry edits, disturbances, design components, map overlays, and time-series probes are not afterthoughts. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:15 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:16 ` ## Tavakkol And Lynett 2017 `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:17 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:18 ` The 2017 Celeris work is the conceptual ancestor for the GPU-accelerated Boussinesq model. It used earlier GPU shader technology rather than browser WebGPU, but the numerical structure is recognizable in this repository. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:19 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:20 ` Relevant implementation connections: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:21 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:22 ` - The explicit finite-volume update is split from dispersive Boussinesq corrections. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:23 ` - Moving shoreline/wet-dry logic is central to the solver. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:24 ` - Parallel Cyclic Reduction is used for tridiagonal systems in the implicit dispersive solve. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:25 ` - Interactive visualization and rapid scenario feedback are core goals rather than post-processing steps. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:26 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:27 ` ## Tavakkol And Lynett 2020 `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:28 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:29 ` The 2020 Celeris Base work moved the interactive model into a more accessible application environment and emphasized user workflows such as map overlays, gauges, and immersive visualization. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:30 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:31 ` Relevant implementation connections: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:32 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:33 ` - The WebGPU version keeps the same spirit of interactive scenario design, but implements it as a static browser app. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:34 `` - The UI, overlay imagery, time-series gauges, and export features in `main.js`, `File_Loader.js`, `File_Writer.js`, and render shaders continue that workflow direction. ``<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:35 ` - Sponge/boundary handling, visualization, and GPU resource management are as important to the application as the equation kernels. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:36 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:37 ` ## Practical Reading Order `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:38 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:39 ` If you are modifying numerical kernels: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:40 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:41 ` 1. Read the WebGPU paper for the current architecture. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:42 ` 2. Read the earlier Celeris papers for the Boussinesq/PCR and wet-dry lineage. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:43 `` 3. Read `docs/architecture/SIMULATION_PIPELINE.md`. ``<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:44 `` 4. Read the relevant shader docs under `docs/source/shaders/`. ``<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:45 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:46 ` If you are modifying UI, visualization, or scenario loading: `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:47 `  `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:48 ` 1. Read the WebGPU paper for the browser model. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:49 ` 2. Read the 2020 Celeris Base paper for workflow context. `<br>docs/architecture/REFERENCE_PAPERS.md:50 `` 3. Read the docs for `main.js`, `File_Loader.js`, `File_Writer.js`, `Handler_Render.js`, `fragment.wgsl`, and `Copytxf32_txf16.wgsl`. ``<br>논문 계보·응용 목적·읽기 순서 설명이다.<br>코드 수식의 직접 명세가 아니다. 2017·2020과 WebGPU를 같은 구현 판으로 취급하지 않는다. | 계보 문서는 구현 판과 수치식의 직접 대조 근거를 구분하여 사용한다. |

The peak period comes from `incident_wave_T`, the peak direction comes from `incident_wave_direction`, and the generated frequency grid uses about 100 frequencies from `1 / (3 * incident_wave_T)` through `3 / incident_wave_T`. ``<br>docs/source/js/Wave_Generator_js.md:21 `  `<br>docs/source/js/Wave_Generator_js.md:22 `` The TMA path uses nine directions from `incident_wave_direction - 20` degrees through `incident_wave_direction + 20` degrees at 5-degree spacing. When the two boundaries transverse to the incident-wave boundary are periodic, it applies periodic-boundary direction fitting before upload. The fitting uses the active forcing span `boundaryLength - 2 * ds`, matching `BoundaryPass.wgsl` coordinates from index `1` to index `N-2`. Each fitted component selects an integer number of along-boundary waves and sets `k_parallel = sign(k_parallel_raw) * 2*pi*N / activeBoundaryLength`, so the component phase matches at both active ends of the boundary. | CD2-452 | docs/source/js/File_Writer_js.md:14 | C 문서 누락 | docs/source/js/File_Writer_js.md:14 `` - `writeNestedGridBoundaryTimeSeriesData()`: reads one rectangle state's four deferred nested-grid boundary output textures once at the end of capture and writes boundary type `5` compatible text files.
